source: In a multivariate model including the four age acceleration metrics, PROaccel (1.17; 1.00–1.38), mDNAPHENOACCEL (1.20; 1.02–1.42), and mDNAGRIMACCEL (1.31; 1.07–1.60) were significantly predictive of all-cause mortality, but mDNAHORVATHACCEL (0.94; 0.80–1.11) was not.
evidence: The Results section provides specific multivariate model results.

claim: The protein most strongly associated with chronological age in the current study was pleiotrophin (PTN).
source: The protein most strongly associated with chronological age in the current study was pleiotrophin (PTN), which is a heparin-binding growth factor involved in angiogenesis, tumorigenesis, and neuromodulation (Bertram et al., 2019; Souttou et al., 1998).
evidence: The Discussion section states this finding and cites references about PTN function.

claim: PTN was not predictive of either mortality or multimorbidity after adjusting for age.
source: In our study, PTN was not predictive of either mortality or multimorbidity after adjusting for age.
evidence: The Discussion section states this finding.

claim: GDF15 was the most significant age-associated protein predictive of mortality and multimorbidity.
source: GDF15 was the most significant age-associated protein predictive of mortality and multimorbidity.
evidence: The Discussion section states this finding.

claim: GDF15 has been identified as a highly robust senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factor in multiple senescence inducers and cell types.
source: More recently, GDF15 has been identified as a highly robust senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factor in multiple senescence inducers and cell types (Basisty et al., 2020) as well as a driver of senescence-associated colon cancer metastasis (Guo et al., 2019).
evidence: The Discussion section cites references to support this claim about GDF15.

claim: GDF15 is a driver of senescence-associated colon cancer metastasis.
source: More recently, GDF15 has been identified as a highly robust senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factor in multiple senescence inducers and cell types (Basisty et al., 2020) as well as a driver of senescence-associated colon cancer metastasis (Guo et al., 2019).
evidence: The Discussion section cites a reference to support this claim about GDF15.

claim: 11 proteins (GDF15, MMP1, STC1, IGFBP2, IGFBP4, TIMP1, TIMP2, CST3, CTSB, CLEC11A, and POSTN) are both core SASP components and also associated with all-cause mortality and multimorbidity.
source: Among the most robust SASP components we identified 11 proteins in this study - GDF15, MMP1, STC1, IGFBP2, IGFBP4, TIMP1, TIMP2, CST3, CTSB, CLEC11A, and POSTN – which are both core SASP components (secreted by multiple types of senescent cells and senescence inducers) and also associated with all-cause mortality and multimorbidity.
evidence: The Discussion section identifies these proteins and their associations.

claim: IL-6, a classical SASP factor in multiple senescent cell types, was also associated with all-cause mortality.
source: IL-6, a classical SASP factor in multiple senescent cell types (Coppé et al., 2008), was also associated with all-cause mortality.
evidence: The Discussion section states this finding and cites a reference.

claim: MMP1 is a biomarker for several cancers, pulmonary fibrosis and potentially Alzheimer's disease.
source: In addition to aging, MMP1 is a biomarker for several cancers, pulmonary fibrosis and potentially Alzheimer's disease (Bhat et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2016b; Rosas et al., 2008), whereas STC1 is a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for cancers, pulmonary fibrosis, renal ischemia/reperfusion injury and Alzheimer's disease (Chang et al., 2015; Ohkouchi et al., 2015; Pan et al., 2015; Shahim et al., 2017).
evidence: The Discussion section cites references to support this claim about MMP1.

claim: STC1 is a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for cancers, pulmonary fibrosis, renal ischemia/reperfusion injury and Alzheimer's disease.
source: In addition to aging, MMP1 is a biomarker for several cancers, pulmonary fibrosis and potentially Alzheimer's disease (Bhat et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2016b; Rosas et al., 2008), whereas STC1 is a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for cancers, pulmonary fibrosis, renal ischemia/reperfusion injury and Alzheimer's disease (Chang et al., 2015; Ohkouchi et al., 2015; Pan et al., 2015; Shahim et al., 2017).
evidence: The Discussion section cites references to support this claim about STC1.

claim: A peak shift in the proteome was found at 78 years of age, replicating the same exact timing of the INTERVAL and LonGenity study.
source: We explored whether similar patterns can be observed in the InCHIANTI study, and strikingly we found a peak shift in the proteome in the eighth decade at 78 years of age replicating the same exact timing of the INTERVAL and LonGenity study.
evidence: The Discussion section states this replication finding.

claim: Circulating NPPB reduces blood pressure and plasma volume through its effect on the adrenal gland, kidney, brain and vasculature.
source: Circulating NPPB reduces blood pressure and plasma volume through its effect on the adrenal gland, kidney, brain and vasculature (Levin et al., 1998).
evidence: The Discussion section cites a reference to support this claim about NPPB function.

claim: Circulating NPPB levels are found at high concentrations in patients with heart failure and was shown to be a useful diagnostic tool in an acute setting.
source: Circulating NPPB levels are found at high concentrations in patients with heart failure and was shown to be a useful diagnostic tool in an acute setting (Davis et al., 1994; Gardner, 2003).
evidence: The Discussion section cites references to support this claim about NPPB as a biomarker.

claim: A genome-wide association study of circulating NPPB identified variants in the NPPB locus, and these variants were also associated with lower systolic and diastolic blood pressure as well as lower risk of hypertension.
source: A genome-wide association study of circulating NPPB identified a variants in the NPPB locus, and these variants were also associated with lower systolic and diastolic blood pressure as well as lower risk of hypertension (Newton-Cheh et al., 2009).
evidence: The Discussion section cites a reference to support this genetic claim.

claim: MMP12 is a metalloprotease produced primarily by macrophages and is involved in inflammation and tissue damage.
source: MMP12 is a metalloprotease produced primarily by macrophages and is involved in inflammation and tissue damage (Shapiro et al., 1993).
evidence: The Discussion section cites a reference to support this claim about MMP12 function.

claim: While circulating levels of MMP12 have been linked to increased risk of cardiovascular disease, genetically increased MMP12 has been linked to reduced cardiovascular disease risk.
source: While circulating levels of MMP12 have been linked to increased risk of cardiovascular disease, genetically increased MMP12 has been linked to reduced cardiovascular disease risk in the current report as well as others (Sun et al., 2018; Chong et al., 2019).
evidence: The Discussion section cites references to support this claim about MMP12 associations.

claim: PI3 is a skin-derived serine protease inhibitor that plays an important role in hydrolyzing connective tissue components including elastin and collagen through the inhibition of elastase.
source: PI3 is a skin-derived serine protease inhibitor that plays an important role in hydrolyzing connective tissue components including elastin and collagen through the inhibition of elastase (Schalkwijk et al., 1990; Wiedow et al., 1990).
evidence: The Discussion section cites references to support this claim about PI3 function.

claim: PI3 has been linked to lung tissue repair and is a candidate biomarker for lung diseases including acute respiratory lung disease and asthma.
source: PI3 has also been linked to lung tissue repair and is a candidate biomarker for lung diseases including acute respiratory lung disease and asthma (Wang et al., 2017; Tsai et al., 2016), as well as modulator of inflammation through the inhibition of neutrophil derived elastases (Alam et al., 2012).
evidence: The Discussion section cites references to support this claim about PI3 as a biomarker.

claim: SMOC1 has been identified as the candidate gene underlying the signal on chromosome 14 in genome-wide association studies of bone mineral density and osteoporosis.
source: Our results are consistent with results from genome-wide association studies of bone mineral density and osteoporosis, where SMOC1 has been identified as the candidate gene underlying the signal on chromosome 14 (Zhang et al., 2014; Qiu et al., 2019).
evidence: The Discussion section cites references to support this genetic claim.

claim: SMOC1 knockout results in disruption of ocular and limb development through reduction in interdigital apoptosis and disruption in BMP signaling in animal studies.
source: Animal studies have shown that SMOC1 knockout results in disruption of ocular and limb development through reduction in interdigital apoptosis and disruption in BMP signaling.
evidence: The Discussion section states this finding from animal studies.

claim: GHR knockout animals display disproportional bone growth and lower bone mineral density.
source: GHR knockout animals display disproportional bone growth and lower bone mineral density (Sjögren et al., 2000).
evidence: The Discussion section cites a reference to support this claim about GHR.

claim: Administration of growth hormone has been shown to improve bone mineral density in postmenopausal women.
source: In humans, administration of growth hormone has been shown to improve bone mineral density in postmenopausal women (Joseph et al., 2008).
evidence: The Discussion section cites a reference to support this claim about growth hormone.

claim: The proteomic age signature developed by the authors is strikingly similar to another proteomic age signature created in a geographically distinct population by Lehallier and colleagues.
source: What was surprising is that the proteomic age signature developed by our group is strikingly similar to another proteomic age signature created in a geographically distinct population by Lehallier and colleagues (Lehallier et al., 2019).
evidence: The Discussion section cites a reference to support this comparison.

claim: Subjects who were predicted to be older than their chronological age had higher prevalence of comorbidities, more rapid increase in co-morbidities over time, and higher risk of all-cause mortality.
source: Using this proteomic signature, subjects who were predicted to be older than their chronological age had higher prevalence of comorbidities, more rapid increase in co-morbidities over time, and higher risk of all-cause mortality.
evidence: The Discussion section summarizes the findings about proteomic age acceleration.

claim: PROaccel performed better than mDNAHORVATHACCEL, but was outperformed by mDNAPHENOACCEL and mDNAGRIMACCEL in predicting all-cause mortality.
source: PROaccel performed better than mDNAHORVATHACCEL, but was outperformed by mDNAPHENOACCEL and mDNAGRIMACCEL.
evidence: The Discussion section compares the performance of different aging clocks.

claim: Creating a proteomic signature of aging phenotypes, rather than chronological age, could result in a more robust proteomic biomarker for aging.
source: This would suggest that creating a proteomic signature of aging phenotypes, rather than chronological age, could result in a more robust proteomic biomarker for aging and should be explored in future studies.
evidence: The Discussion section suggests this as a future direction based on the findings.

claim: The InCHIANTI study is a population-based epidemiological study aimed at evaluating factors that influence mobility in the older population living in the Chianti region in Tuscany, Italy.
source: The InCHIANTI study is a population-based epidemiological study aimed at evaluating factors that influence mobility in the older population living in the Chianti region in Tuscany, Italy.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the study design.

claim: 1616 residents were selected from the population registry of Greve in Chianti and Bagno a Ripoli.
source: Briefly, 1616 residents were selected from the population registry of Greve in Chianti (a rural area: 11,709 residents with 19.3% of the population older than 65 years of age) and Bagno a Ripoli (Antella village near Florence; 4704 inhabitants, with 20.3% older than 65 years of age).
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides specific sampling information.

claim: The participation rate was 90% (n = 1453) and subjects' age ranged between 21 and 102 years.
source: The participation rate was 90% (n = 1453) and subjects' age ranged between 21 and 102 years.
evidence: The Materials and methods section provides specific participation data.

claim: Proteomic profiles for 1322 SOMAmers were assessed using the 1.3 k SOMAscan Assay.
source: Proteomic profiles for 1322 SOMAmers were assessed using the 1.3 k SOMAscan Assay at the Trans-NIH Center for Human Immunology, Autoimmunity, and Inflammation (CHI), National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, National Institutes of Health (Bethesda, MD, USA) using the same methods as previously published (Tanaka et al., 2018).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the proteomic assessment method and cites a reference.

claim: Out of the 1322 SOMAmer reagents, 12 hybridization controls, four viral proteins and 5 SOMAmers that were reported to be non-specific were removed, thus leaving 1301 SOMAmer reagents in the final analysis.
source: Out of the 1322 SOMAmer reagents, 12 hybridization controls, four viral proteins (HPV type 16, HPV type 18, isolate BEN, isolate LW123) and 5 SOMAmers that were reported to be non-specific (P05186; ALPL, P09871; C1S, Q14126; DSG2, Q93038; TNFRSF25, Q9NQC3; RTN4) were removed, thus leaving 1301 SOMAmer reagents in the final analysis.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the data filtering process.

claim: Genomic DNA was extracted from buffy coat samples (white blood cells) collected at the baseline visit and methylation status of ~480,000 CpG were assessed with Illumina Infinium HumanMethylation450 BeadChip.
source: In brief, genomic DNA was extracted from buffy coat samples (white blood cells) collected at the baseline visit and methylation status of ~480,000 CpG were assessed with Illumina Infinium HumanMethylation450 BeadChip (Illumina Inc, San Diego, CA) using manufacturer's protocol.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the methylation assessment method.

claim: After filtering CpG with cross-reactive probes, on polymorphic position, and on X or Y chromosomes, 472,139 markers in 460 subjects with both proteomic and methylation data were used for analysis.
source: After filtering CpG with cross-reactive probes, on polymorphic position, and on X or Y chromosomes, 472,139 markers in 460 subjects with both proteomic and methylation data were used for analysis.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the final dataset after filtering.
